text:
Maria Chen: quick follow-up from the SDK surface RFC — we didn't land on a cross-language pattern for pagination + retries. how should python/ts/go behave for streaming generators when transient errors occur?

Samir Patel: short answer: make retries transport-layer by default, but provide hooks for iterator-level resume. more detail below.

Lee Kim: agree with transport-layer first. if the transport can replay safely (idempotent GET-like pagination), automatic retry is fine. trouble is stateful streams (chat/streaming completion) and partial-page tokens.

Joanna: for pagination specifically, can we standardize on a resume token in the iterator API? e.g. iterator.next() raises RetryableError and library can optionally call transport.resume(token)

Samir Patel: proto idea for Python:
```py
# high level iterator
for item in client.list_items(page_size=100):
    process(item)

# iterator carries last_seen_token, user can opt to persist it
```
If transport raises, the client will retry fetching the current page unless token indicates partial-page progress.

Lee Kim: Typescript needs to work with both async iterator and streaming callbacks. proposal: expose two primitives:
- asyncIterable(listParams) -> AsyncIterable<T> (resumable via token)
- stream(listParams, onData) -> cancelable stream (no automatic resume)

Joanna: Go: channel-based iterators usually can't be resumed easily. better to return a pager object with Next(ctx) (returns item, resumeToken). Next can return a special Retryable error so caller can decide.

Maria Chen: ok tradeoffs:
- automatic retry for whole-page failures: good UX for simple GET-style pagination
- automatic retry for per-item failures inside a streaming callback: risky (duplicate items or partial side effects)

Samir Patel: implementation details:
- transport should attach idempotency metadata (request id + resume token) to allow safe replay.
- default retry policy: retry on 5xx and network errors, bounded backoff, respect user deadline/context.

Joanna: tests we need:
- simulated flaky transport that drops one RPC mid-page -> ensure iterator either retries whole page or surfaces retryable error depending on language config
- partial-page commit (server returns items + next_token) then error on next page -> ensure next run continues from token.

Lee Kim: small API sketches (typescript):
```ts
// resumable pager
const pager = client.listItems({ pageSize: 50 });
for await (const item of pager) { /* ... */ }
// or explicit
const { items, nextToken } = await client.fetchPage(token);
```
Make clear in docs which primitive auto-retries.

Maria Chen: UX decisions: default to automatic whole-page retries for all languages, opt-out flag for "no-retry". streaming callbacks default to no automatic resume; expose resume token in callback context.

infra-ops: deploy-bot: deploy status: sdk-retries-v2 feature branch deployed to staging (build #542). integration tests: 18/22 passing, failing tests are flaky transport sims.

Samir Patel: follow-ups:
- add resume_token field to pager metadata across SDKs
- document idempotency expectations for server implementers (when is safe to replay)
- add small example for Go showing how to persist token and resume after failure

Joanna: timeline: get agreement here, then I'll open follow-up RFC + language-specific PRs. aim to land core behavior in 2 weeks.

Maria Chen: sounds good. last question: should SDKs surface a unified RetryableError class/name across languages? makes testing and detection easier.

Lee Kim: yes, surface a semantic error (e.g. ClientRetryableError) but map to idiomatic language types (Error subclass in py, custom Error in ts, sentinel error var in go).

Samir Patel: +1. I'll draft a compatibility matrix and minimal change list for each SDK.

Maria Chen: thanks — can everyone react with :thumbsup: if they agree and I'll mark RFC follow-up.

dev-bot: thread pinned to #eng-platform for tracking.
